note: Always with a negative: 아무런 ... 없다/않다.

ex.en: There's no problem at all.
I haven't heard anything from Ji-woo.

ex.s: 이 약은 아무런 맛이 안 나요.
ex.en: This medicine has no taste at all.
The kids are playing at the playground.
There's a playground in front of our apartment.
It's raining, so nobody's at the playground.
Thanks for the good suggestion.

ex.s: 민호 씨가 여행 가자고 제안을 했어요.
ex.en: Minho suggested that we go on a trip.

ex.s: 그 회사에서 같이 일하자는 제안을 받았어요.
ex.en: That company offered me a job.

ex.s: 일 년 중에 이때가 제일 바빠요.
ex.en: This is the busiest time of the year.
Right at that moment, the phone rang.

ex.s: 이 사진 봐요. 이때 우리 정말 어렸네요.
ex.en: Look at this photo. We were so young back then.
Our team communicates well.
I don't communicate well with my parents.
These days I communicate with friends by text.
Is this ring gold?
Gold prices have gone up a lot lately.
I gave my grandma a gold necklace.
I can feel the baby moving inside me.
The cat moves really fast.
The characters in this game move naturally.
My older brother works for a big company.
Do big companies pay well?

ex.s: 저는 대기업보다 작은 회사가 더 좋아요.
ex.en: I prefer a small company to a big corporation.

note: A bit formal; casual speech usually uses 드디어.

ex.en: The exams are finally over.
We finally bought our own home.

ex.s: 두 시간 기다려서 마침내 비행기를 탔어요.
ex.en: After waiting two hours, we finally boarded the plane.
The sandcastle my kid built fell down.
All our plans fell apart because of the rain.
My heart sank when I heard that.
I give up my seat to elderly people on the subway.
A lot of elderly people live in this neighborhood.
That hospital has many elderly patients.

en: to fall for, be charmed by

ex.en: It was love at first sight.
I fell in love with that restaurant's food.
Mina was charmed by Seoul's night view.
My income is a bit low this month.
I'm spending more than I earn.
This fruit is imported, so it's expensive.
I'm looking for a stable job.
My father is stable after his surgery.
The Wi-Fi here is stable.
I'm staying in Seoul for a week.
Which hotel are you staying at?

ex.s: 지호 씨는 이모 집에 며칠 머물렀어요.
ex.en: Jiho stayed at his aunt's place for a few days.
My little brother is pretending to sleep.
Don't pretend you don't know.
I pretended to know during the meeting.

note: Casual word; fine with kids and pets.

ex.en: The puppy pooped on the street.

ex.s: 아기가 똥 쌌어요. 기저귀 좀 주세요.
ex.en: The baby pooped. Please pass me a diaper.
Bird poop landed on my car.
Smoking is banned in this park.
Mom banned video games at night.

ex.s: 우리 회사는 회의 중에 휴대폰을 금지해요.
ex.en: Our company bans phones during meetings.
Look at that!
How much is that one, too?
This one tastes better than that one.

ex.s: 어제 방탈출 게임에서 한 시간 만에 탈출했어요.
ex.en: Yesterday we got out of the escape room in an hour.
The hamster escaped from its box.
I want to escape this heat soon.
Everyone in my family is tall.
I cleaned the whole house over the weekend.
In winter it's really dry inside the house.
That was a good call.
I'll leave the decision to Sofía.
Don't judge people by their appearance.
I want to go to grad school next year.
My older sister is in grad school.
Grad school tuition is too expensive.
The rumor has already spread everywhere.
A cold is going around the office.
The smell of bread is spreading from the kitchen.
This yoga pose is too hard.
You move really fast.
I memorized all the dance moves.
How many people is the reservation for?

ex.s: 이 방은 최대 인원이 네 명이에요.
ex.en: This room holds up to four people.
More people are coming to the meeting now.

note: 미소를 짓다 = to smile. Everyday speech often uses 웃음/웃다.

ex.en: The baby's smile is really cute.
Kevin always has a smile on his face.
That employee had a really friendly smile.
There's tension between the team members.
My husband and I have had some conflict lately.
This drama is about family conflict.
Shall we see a movie at the theater?
Let's meet in front of the theater.
Theater popcorn is too expensive.

note: Often with -(으)ㄹ지도 모르다 or -(으)ㄹ 수도 있다.

ex.en: It might rain tomorrow.
I might be a little late.

ex.s: 어쩌면 그게 더 나을 것 같아요.
ex.en: Maybe that would be better.
The last scene of that movie was memorable.
Your presentation was really impressive.
What was the most memorable place on Jeju?
In an emergency, call this number.
Where's the emergency exit?
I keep some emergency cash in my wallet.
Are you okay? Did you get hurt?
I hurt my leg playing soccer.
Be careful. You could get hurt.
I politely turned down the invitation.
Jimin turned down my request.
I decided to turn down that company's offer.
The moving truck comes in the morning.
I bought tacos from a food truck.
There are lots of trucks on the highway.
Is there a store near here?
For here?
Those shoes aren't in the store right now.

en: to be put in, be filled with
note: Passive of 담다 (to put in, fill).

ex.s: 이 사진에 추억이 많이 담겨 있어요.
ex.en: This photo holds a lot of memories.
The side dishes are neatly packed in the lunch box.
Mom's letter was full of love.
Our team won 3 to 1.
I really want to win this game.
Did Korea win yesterday?
I'm embarrassed to sing in front of people.
The child was shy and hid behind her mom.
I made a mistake and was so embarrassed.

note: For night dreams, 꿈을 꾸다 is more common.

ex.en: As a kid, I dreamed of being a singer.
I dream of living by the sea after retirement.
Lately I've been dreaming of traveling the world.
Now isn't the right time.
At this price, it's reasonable.
I don't have suitable clothes for an interview.
The room is a bit small.

ex.s: 이 길은 너무 좁아서 운전하기 힘들어요.
ex.en: This road is so narrow it's hard to drive.
The airplane seats were cramped.
The stars are shining tonight.
The ring really sparkles.
The kids' eyes are sparkling.
My older brother does cancer research at a university.
I've been working on tasty recipes lately.
I researched good restaurants carefully before the trip.
How long does it take to get there?
Now let's move on to the next place.
Getting around by subway is the fastest.
Do you offer same-day delivery?
If you cancel on the day, there's no refund.
How about a day trip to Jeju?
Our coach is really strict.
My son's soccer coach is kind.
The coach says there's no practice today.
My college years were the best days of my youth.
Dad says he's still young at heart.
I like coming-of-age movies.
That person gives a good impression.
What was your impression of Korea?
Did you hear about the bus fare increase?
Sorry, I stepped on your foot.
Don't step on the wet floor.
I slammed on the brakes.
My back hurts because of bad posture.
Sit up straight in your chair.
Ji-woo has a great attitude at work.
I make YouTube content.
There's a lot of fun content these days.
I'm picking out shows for the kids to watch.

note: Always with a negative; a bit formal. Speech often uses 절대.

ex.en: It's by no means an easy job.
I'll never forget that day.
I'll never give up.
My daughter wants to become a scientist.
Wei's father is a scientist.
They say scientists have developed a new medicine.
Have you set the wedding date?

ex.s: 마시기 전에 우유 날짜 확인해 보세요.
ex.en: Check the date on the milk before you drink it.
I'd like to change my reservation to another date.
I bought the latest phone.
This laptop is the newest model.

ex.s: 요즘 최신 영화 중에 볼 만한 거 있어요?
ex.en: Are there any new movies worth watching?

note: For children growing taller, 자라다 is more common.

ex.en: Kids grow up really fast.
Our company has grown a lot.

ex.s: 이번 일로 많이 성장한 것 같아요.
ex.en: I feel like I grew a lot through this.

ex.s: 이번 학기에 수업을 다섯 개 들어요.
ex.en: I'm taking five classes this semester.
When does next semester start?
When the semester ends, I'm going on a trip.

ex.s: 자막 없이 영화를 볼 수 있어요.
ex.en: I can watch movies without subtitles.
Are there English subtitles?
Please turn on the subtitles.
You can substitute honey for sugar.

ex.s: 이 일은 AI가 대체할 수 없어요.
ex.en: AI can't replace this job.
We'll replace today's meeting with an email.

note: Usually 깜짝 놀라다; 깜짝 파티 = surprise party.

ex.en: You startled me!
We threw a surprise party for my friend's birthday.
The sound of the door made me jump.
My bag is too heavy.
I'll carry the heavy stuff.
I ate a big lunch, so I feel sluggish.
I've been so busy I have no time to breathe.
Leave with plenty of time to spare.

ex.s: 이번 달은 돈에 여유가 좀 있어요.
ex.en: I have a little extra money this month.

note: Used like an adverb before adjectives.

ex.en: This restaurant is relatively cheap.
It's relatively warm today.
This exam was fairly easy.
Dad drove over.
I drove a car for the first time after getting my license.
My uncle drives a truck.
How did the salary negotiation go?
Negotiating the house price isn't easy.

ex.s: 지금 아이하고 게임 시간 협상 중이에요.
ex.en: I'm negotiating gaming time with my kid right now.
I lost my wallet, so I went to the police station.
Where's the police station?
There's a café next to the police station.

note: Medical word; in casual talk just say 아파요.

ex.en: My back pain is bad.
How long have you had the pain?

ex.s: 이 약 먹으면 통증이 줄어들 거예요.
ex.en: This medicine will ease the pain.
My phone battery died.
I only have ten percent battery.
We need to change the remote's batteries.

note: 사기를 당하다 = to get scammed; 사기꾼 = scammer.

ex.en: That text is a scam.
I got scammed online.
This price is a total rip-off!
Could you call the manager, please?
Our manager is really nice.
I have a meeting with my manager this afternoon.
I want to be rich.
Diego's uncle is rich.
It's payday, so I feel rich.
I'll start with the bottom line.
We haven't reached a conclusion yet.
The bottom line is we meet again tomorrow.
I got my tooth treated at the dentist.

ex.s: 이 병은 쉽게 치료할 수 있어요.
ex.en: This illness can be treated easily.
The vet treated the puppy's leg.
I'm going to see a play this weekend.
My daughter is in the school play.
I was in the drama club in college.
My older brother keeps picking on me.
Mosquitoes bothered me all night.
You must not bully classmates at school.
My flight was delayed, so I got compensation.
I took a vacation as a reward for working hard.
My package was damaged, so I asked for compensation.

note: Also 화가 나다. 화났어요 = I'm angry.

ex.en: Why are you angry?
My friend got angry because I was late.
Something really infuriating happened today.
Are you two a couple?
My boyfriend and I got matching rings.
There are lots of couples at this restaurant.
Paying taxes is a duty.
Wearing a seatbelt is mandatory.
Taking care of children is a parent's duty.
Take good care of your health.
I manage this team's budget.
How do you take care of your skin?

note: Used for any pet dog, not only puppies.

ex.en: Do you have a dog?
I walk my dog every morning.
The puppy is so cute!
Housing is expensive in big cities.
I prefer the countryside to big cities.
Chicago is a big city.
Welcome! Come on in.
There's a party to welcome the new employee.
You're welcome anytime.
The kids shouted, "It's Santa!"
We shouted our team's name at the stadium.
I shouted for help.

note: Also a counter: 케이크 한 조각.

ex.en: Would you like a slice of cake?
I ate two slices of pizza.
The plate broke, and there are pieces on the floor.
Please turn to the next page.
I'll hand this task over to Minho.
I missed the deadline.
Please have a seat.
Is this chair free?
My new office chair is comfortable.
Stay healthy!
Grandma is still in good health.
These days I try to eat healthy food.
There's a sale at the department store.
There's a food court in the department store's basement.
The department store is too crowded on weekends.

note: Careful: also crude slang for "to die."

ex.en: I dug through my bag, but my keys aren't there.
I rummaged through the fridge and found something to eat.
I'm as fit as young people.

note: Common exaggeration for a terrible situation.

ex.en: The subway at rush hour is hell.
Exam period was absolute hell.
Dieting feels like hell.
That player is a baseball legend.
There's an interesting legend about this mountain.
My grandpa is a legend in the neighborhood.
It's a work-related email.
I have a question about the trip.
These days I read books about health.

en: to stand out, catch the eye
note: Usually 눈에 띄다. Don't confuse with 띠다.

ex.en: That red coat stands out.
You've gotten noticeably slimmer lately.

ex.s: 간판이 작아서 눈에 잘 안 띄어요.
ex.en: The sign is small, so it's hard to notice.
Seats are limited.
This discount is only for today.
Quantities are limited, so you have to buy fast.
Do you like action movies?
This game has amazing action.

ex.s: 그 배우는 액션 장면을 직접 해요.
ex.en: That actor does his own action scenes.
That singer is internationally famous.
I want to work at an international company.
This festival is an international event.
I'm under a lot of pressure at work.
I checked the tire pressure before the trip.
I feel pressure in my ears on the plane.
Did you watch the awards show last night?
Year-end awards shows are too long.
My daughter got a prize at the school awards ceremony.
